decision: The exact Fricke premise, Q-defined modular quotient, chosen Tate constituent, coefficient descent of Hom, and same-field isogeny consumer match the inspected source interfaces.

nine_obligations.name: source_hypotheses
nine_obligations.required: A normalized weight-two common Hecke eigenform on a group between Gamma1(N) and Gamma0(N); Fricke-stable full conjugate span for Shimura’s zeta conclusion.
nine_obligations.constructed: The finite twist has already been absorbed and the final normalized primitive newform f of level N and nebentypus epsilon has been chosen.
nine_obligations.why_match: Use Gamma1(N), not the easier Gamma0(N) alternative. Li’s actual arbitrary-character newform relation supplies the extra Fricke premise.

nine_obligations.name: constructed_objects
nine_obligations.required: An actual Q-defined quotient A_f of the same J1(N) with the relevant differential and Euler-factor data.
nine_obligations.constructed: Shimura supplies q:J1(N)→A_f over Q, dim A_f=[K_f:Q], coefficient-field endomorphisms, and the pullback differential span of every coefficient conjugate.
nine_obligations.why_match: The quotient is geometric and Q-defined by the source theorem. It is not inferred solely from equal Frobenius traces or constructed over a cyclotomic coefficient field.

nine_obligations.name: domain_index_coverage
nine_obligations.required: Every coefficient embedding, not just the embedding selected by Pan, must enter the product Euler factors and Fricke span.
nine_obligations.constructed: Use all embeddings of K_f into C and, after a finite splitting coefficient extension, into Qbar_5.
nine_obligations.why_match: Shimura supplies all conjugates before its conditional zeta assertion. Li’s primitive decomposition and Theorem 5 show each conjugate stays primitive at N by conjugating a hypothetical lower-level source back. This avoids circular use of the zeta conclusion.

nine_obligations.name: transition_comparison_maps
nine_obligations.required: Pass from Li’s slash operation to Shimura’s map, then from Euler factors to a genuine representation constituent using named comparison results.
nine_obligations.constructed: At weight two h(-1/(Nz))/z²=N(h|H_N)(z). Compare the whole Tate module of A_f with the sum of conjugate modular representations, using Chebotarev and the semisimple-character theorem.
nine_obligations.why_match: The scalar N does not affect span stability. Faltings gives Tate semisimplicity; equality of total characters identifies semisimplifications through the finite-dimensional image algebra. The chosen known irreducible r5 then occurs.
nine_obligations.evidence: Li p.296; Shimura p.526; Faltings Satz 3; Milne IV Lemma 3.9

nine_obligations.name: identity_of_consumed_object
nine_obligations.required: The exact r5 from the corrected QM action must be a common constituent over the actual field Lprime.
nine_obligations.constructed: Over G_Lprime the correction is trivial and V5(A) is r5 direct-sum r5. The same r5 is in V5(A_f), hence in V5(J1(N)) after semisimple splitting of the quotient.
nine_obligations.why_match: This uses the selected Pan embedding inside the whole direct sum, not an unsupported labeling of individual coefficient factors from a product polynomial. Restriction is to the existing Lprime, not a newly enlarged number field.

nine_obligations.name: coefficients_normalizations
nine_obligations.required: Keep Tate/cohomological duals, finite coefficient extensions, Fricke normalization and nebentypus distinct.
nine_obligations.constructed: r5 is the Tate constituent, while r5 dual is the H1 constituent. Li maps epsilon to its conjugate; complex conjugation permutes all embeddings, even for a non-Galois coefficient field.
nine_obligations.why_match: No single form is assumed to be a Fricke eigenvector, no algebraicity of its Fricke scalar is needed, and no bound on coefficient degree is imposed. Invariants in the finite-dimensional Hom space commute with coefficient extension.

nine_obligations.name: local_conditions
nine_obligations.required: The representation comparison needs equality away from one finite bad set and the same arithmetic/geometric Frobenius convention.
nine_obligations.constructed: Shimura’s good-prime product Euler factors match the conjugate modular factors after consistently using the Tate convention; omit bad primes and the coefficient prime.
nine_obligations.why_match: Chebotarev density and continuity extend trace equality. Missing finitely many local factors do not obstruct the comparison. This step makes no new conductor claim at omitted primes.
nine_obligations.evidence: Shimura Theorem 1 final clause; compatible-trace-convention; preceding conductor review

nine_obligations.name: exceptional_cases
nine_obligations.required: Handle nontrivial nebentypus, unbounded coefficient degree, the published Faltings correction, and coefficient extension versus field of definition.
nine_obligations.constructed: All are allowed. Faltings 1984 corrects the preceding height-tower assertion to eventual stationarity, and says this suffices for later results.
nine_obligations.why_match: Satz 3/4 semisimplicity and End remain available. Apply End to A×J and take the off-diagonal block for Hom. A finite coefficient extension is not a base-field extension. Milne’s imperfect-field footnote is irrelevant over Lprime.
nine_obligations.evidence: Faltings 1983 p.360 and erratum p.381; Milne I Proposition 10.1

nine_obligations.name: downstream_consumption
nine_obligations.required: Produce an actual nonzero Lprime-homomorphism A→J and an Lprime-isogeny A×Z→J, as used by the height argument.
nine_obligations.constructed: The common constituent yields a nonzero invariant Tate Hom after coefficient extension; descent gives one over Q5. Faltings identifies it with geometric Hom tensored Q5. Absolute simplicity gives finite kernel onto its image; Poincare supplies a complement over Lprime.
nine_obligations.why_match: This names the exact theorems bridging representations to geometry. The J_H variant consumes its separately constructed Q-isogeny factor A_f of J_H; this review does not silently certify that quotient producer or subsequent height bounds.
